minutes.headline: Assessors approved a deed-problem letter, a motor-vehicle signature stamp, and minutes; they are still working out neighborhood fixes and overlay.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors caught up on a backlog of minutes, approved a standard letter asking homeowners to clarify unclear deeds, and approved using a stamp instead of signatures on motor vehicle excise certificates. Most discussion was the principal assessor's status report, a CAI/Vision parcel-mapping problem, a senior means-tested exemption, neighborhood and site-index review, and the FY26 overlay recommendation. The board then moved to executive session.

budget_items.what_was_said: Commitment number one of 25 is being mailed on Feb 20 with a stated bill count; commitment seven of 24 adds further bills.

A refund total was read for the board's review and signing.
An amount is in the proposed budget under capital for the neighborhood and site-index work, as non-recurring; it will probably be needed again in later years.
Other towns' asset limits differ widely; the board will set its own income and asset limits. The exemption cannot exceed a share of the tax levy.
The overlay balance and unspent amount were discussed, along with conflicting figures from the accountant; the board must recommend an overlay amount to the town manager.
Town counsel suggested the town could pay for title searches, whose cost depends on how far back they go.
Forms were mailed to businesses for FY2026.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to adopt a drafted letter to send homeowners when there is a problem with a deed; the third vote was not clearly captioned.
The board voted to allow a stamp instead of a signature on motor vehicle excise abatement certificates; real estate certificates still need signatures.
The board left the FY26 overlay unresolved and asked the principal assessor to bring a recommendation with analysis to the next meeting.
On the senior means-tested exemption, the board favored an early September deadline, a one-year look-back on the circuit breaker return, and anonymous control numbers.
The chair will rewrite the Clause 41 and 17 draft after town counsel's feedback; the board kept March 5th, with March 12th as the fallback if there is no quorum.

why_it_matters: The overlay is the reserve that covers property tax abatements, and the amount the board recommends to the town manager feeds into how much the town must raise through the tax levy.

The deed letter and the senior exemption draft decide how homeowners with unclear deeds are contacted, and who could qualify for a means-tested tax break, with income and asset limits still to be set.
watch_next: The March 5th Board of Assessors meeting (tentatively March 12th if there is no quorum), where the overlay recommendation is due.
The chair's rewritten Clause 41 and 17 income and asset draft, to be sent before the next meeting.
